original_question: Over all edge-colourings of the hypercube Q_n with two colours, determine the largest possible average, over all antipodal vertex pairs v and v-bar, of the minimum number of colour changes needed along a path from v to v-bar. One may ask the same question with the paths restricted to be geodesics.
target_in_paper: Section 8, Question 8.3 ("Antipodal paths in Q_n with few colour changes")
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s averaged variant of the antipodal-path problem: a 2-edge-colouring of the hypercube Q_n, antipodal endpoints v and its antipode, minimization of the number of colour changes along a connecting path, maximization over all colourings, and the separately mentioned geodesic-only version.
missing_details: The official target is Question 8.3, which is a variant of Conjecture 8.1/Question 8.2; it is not the original one-pair existence conjecture.
The colouring is specifically a red-blue colouring of the edges of Q_n.
The average is written explicitly in the paper as (1/2^n) times the sum over all vertices v in Q_n of the minimum number of colour changes on a path from v to its antipode.
To make the question stand-alone, one should define the antipode of v as the vertex differing from v in every coordinate (equivalently, the bitwise complement).
One should define a colour change as an index at which two consecutive edges of the path have different colours.
The minimization is over all v-to-antipode paths in Q_n; only afterwards does the paper note the analogous variant where the minimum is restricted to geodesics.
If the geodesic variant is mentioned, geodesic should be defined exactly as in the nearby context: a shortest path in Q_n, equivalently one in which no direction is repeated.
The quantity being asked for is a function of n: for each n, maximize that average over all red-blue edge-colourings of Q_n.
refined_question: For each n, among all red-blue edge-colourings of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n, determine the maximum possible value of (1/2^n) sum over v in Q_n of m(v), where m(v) denotes the minimum number of colour changes along any path in Q_n from v to its antipode (the vertex differing from v in every coordinate).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if v is chosen uniformly at random from V(Q_n), how large can the expected minimum number of colour changes on a path from v to its antipode be, maximized over all red-blue edge-colourings of Q_n? The paper then separately notes the analogous version with the minimum restricted to geodesic paths.
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s Section 8 averaged variant, namely Question 8.3, rather than the stronger existence statements Conjecture 8.1 or Question 8.2. Section 8 first fixes the ambient setting of red-blue edge-colourings of Q_n, antipodal vertices, and geodesics (Conjecture 8.1). After recalling Question 8.2, the authors explicitly propose the averaged problem in Question 8.3 and rewrite it as a precise normalized sum over all vertices v in Q_n. The paper immediately adds that the same question can also be posed for geodesic paths, so your final sentence matches a genuine nearby variant, but it is not part of the main official statement itself. The surrounding context also explains why this averaged question is intended as an induction-friendly step toward the original antipodal-path conjecture, and notes that a layered colouring gives a lower bound of order sqrt(n), which is part of the motivation for keeping the formulation exactly at the average level rather than broadening it.
